clue.text: Go together, but back in five minutes: 'Won't _____'

definitions.meaning: things that go together fit or suit each other, have a proper place side by side
the sign left on a door, 'Won't ...', fills the blank with two words that mean the speaker will return shortly

explanation.surface: A note pinned to a door promising a quick return, oddly also about things going together.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a fill-in-the-blank: the missing words of the shop-door note, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Two items that go together are said to be matched and fit, each in its rightful place with the other.

clue.text: See 10
Animals ground up, unknown number eaten

indicators.note: the unknown number is swallowed by the other piece, so it goes inside
in a down clue, up means the word for ground is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: ground means soil, earth
N is the mathematician's symbol for an unknown number

explanation.surface: Beasts mashed to bits, with an uncounted quantity of them devoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SOIL into LIOS; 'eaten' puts N inside it before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lions are big cats, an example of the general class of wild animals.

clue.text: Oil pile reaches height that's laughable

parts.note: pile is the raised surface of a carpet or velvet, its nap
HA is the sound of a laugh, something laughable

explanation.surface: A heap of something climbs to a ridiculous altitude, apparently involving oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reaches' and 'that's' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a flammable liquid hydrocarbon, a light oil distilled from petroleum or coal tar.

clue.text: Feline friend of Elliot about to unite

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the two pieces before it round, reading them backwards together

parts.note: a puma is a big wild cat, a feline
ET is the alien befriended by the boy Elliott in the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A big cat and a little alien from the movies are about to join forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses PUMAET as a whole, giving TEAMUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To join up with others in a joint effort is to combine forces, a phrasal verb meaning unite.

clue.text: Old tune blasted out as they leave the stage

parts.note: EX as a prefix means former, old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: a tune blasted out is wrecked and scattered, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: An ancient melody is played loudly as the actors depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasted out' scrambles the four letters of the melody word; 'as' is a link. The surface makes 'Old tune' one phrase, but 'Old' gives the prefix for former.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction meaning that several actors go off, used in scripts.

clue.text: Compose an original scene that's out of this world?

definitions.text: scene that's out of this world?

indicators.note: an original version is new and novel, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An artist is told to create a novel picture with an otherworldly quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges the nine letters of COMPOSE AN; 'Compose' looks like an instruction but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunar landscape is literally a view not of this planet, so the question mark flags the literal reading.

clue.text: Public relations people finally given room, say, to trade in advance

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word people
say signals that the word for room is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: Publicity staff are given space and a chance to sell goods early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link; 'say' makes CELL sound like SELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To presell is to market or sell goods before they are available, a hyphenated verb.

clue.text: Sillier nut who improvised as radio wit

indicators.note: improvised means made up on the spot, so these letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A dafter crackpot made up jokes on the spot as a radio comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improvised' rearranges the thirteen letters of SILLIER NUT WHO. Willie Rushton was an English satirist and cartoonist, a regular panellist on BBC Radio 4's I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This British satirist was famed for his quick humour on radio panel games, a broadcast wit.

clue.text: A short, green jumper in the style of a young Michael Jackson?

definitions.text: style of a young Michael Jackson?

indicators.note: short means a word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a frog is a green creature that jumps

explanation.surface: A trimmed green leaper sports a hairstyle like the young pop star's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts FROG to FRO; 'jumper' looks like a sweater but is the frog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afro is the rounded, bushy hairstyle the boy singer wore in the Jackson 5 days, an example.

clue.text: Why 2 then 16 across?

parts.note: 2 down is a group of big cats, whose collective noun is also a word for vanity, and 16 across is a word meaning a tumble: the clue asks the familiar proverb's question about why one follows the other

explanation.surface: A bare question built from two grid cross-references.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as PRIDE (the lions of 2) COMES BEFORE (then) A FALL (16, DROP), the proverb warning that arrogance leads to disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says arrogance is followed by humiliation, the reason one thing comes after the other.

clue.text: Cheers for model

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
to sit for a portrait is to model

explanation.surface: A toast raised to a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin toast said when drinking, equivalent to the English good health.

clue.text: Artist, one calling from the crow's-nest?

definitions.meaning: Sir Edwin ... was a Victorian painter famous for animals, who also sculpted the lions in London's Trafalgar Square
a lookout high on a ship's mast who sights the shore and calls it out, a seer of land

explanation.surface: A painter doubles as a lookout at the top of a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the name as LAND SEER, the sailor who cries 'Land ho!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Landseer the Victorian painter, and literally someone who spies the shore from the masthead.

clue.text: Sea change seen around Buddhist temple after end of prayers

indicators.note: after places the rest of the wordplay after that final letter
end of picks the final letter of the word prayers
around tells us the word for change surrounds the temple

parts.note: to alter is to change
a wat is a Buddhist temple or monastery in Thailand or Cambodia

explanation.surface: Something shifts in the ocean near a Buddhist shrine once prayers end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the change word round the temple; 'seen' is a link. WAT may be unfamiliar: it is the Thai word for a temple compound.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea consists of brine, so the term for saline water stands for the sea itself.

clue.text: Spooner's tail of dog — chow, we hear?

indicators.note: Spooner's means the first sounds of two words are swapped, in the manner of Rev. Spooner

parts.note: a poodle is a breed of dog
a tip is the end, tail part of something

explanation.surface: Someone describes the end of a dog's tail, then a Chinese breed of dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog's tail end is a POODLE TIP; swapping first letters gives TOODLE PIP. 'chow' sounds like Italian 'ciao', goodbye; chow also suggests the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is old-fashioned British slang for goodbye, which ciao, pronounced chow, also means.

clue.text: See 10
Cut a dash

definitions.meaning: a cut in price or number is a reduction, a fall
a dash of liquid is a tiny amount, a small splash

explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a reduction, as in a price cut, and also a tiny splash, such as a dash of milk.

clue.text: Old royal prince, terribly posh and hip

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, posh, as in U and non-U
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-time prince is described as extremely smart and trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly posh' reads as one phrase but splits: 'terribly' is the anagram signal, and 'posh' must first become U (upper-class) before the pool is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dauphin was the title of the eldest son of the king of France until 1830, a former heir.

clue.text: Cause trouble, as 12 did with each of his 2?

definitions.meaning: to stir up a commotion, create a disturbance ... others

definitions.text: as 12 did with each of his 2?
definitions.meaning: the painter of 12 sculpted the four big cats of 2 down at Nelson's Column, setting each feline in a square full of birds

explanation.surface: A painter is blamed for stirring things up with his big cats.
explanation.walkthrough: Landseer's bronze lions sit in Trafalgar Square, London, long famous for its flocks of pigeons, so he literally put big cats among birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to provoke uproar, like a cat scattering a flock, and literally describes the sculptor's placing of lions.

clue.text: Leader of terrorists has justification for crime …

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of the word terrorists

parts.note: a reason is a justification or grounds for something

explanation.surface: The head of a terror group claims a motive for an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; the ellipsis carries 'crime' into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country or sovereign, an example of a serious offence.

clue.text: … one where a Biblical king punches Paul, perhaps

indicators.note: the king punches into the other piece, getting inside it

parts.note: Paul is an example of a saint, ST
Saul was the first king of Israel in the Bible

explanation.surface: An Old Testament monarch strikes the apostle in a violent scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' picks up 'crime' from the previous clue's ellipsis: an assault is one such crime. 'where' is a link; Paul's earlier name was also Saul, a neat red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Following on from the previous clue, one here stands for a crime, and assault is a criminal offence of violence.

clue.text: Move to cage one as a pet

indicators.note: to cage means to enclose, so the word for move surrounds the one

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone shifts to put a bird in a cage, as a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cage' puts I inside BUDGE; 'as a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgie, short for budgerigar, is a small parakeet commonly kept as a household pet.

clue.text: Leave hair long: half cut and yucky!

parts.note: fur is an animal's hair

indicators.note: half cut means the word long loses its second half, keeping the front

parts.note: ugh is the exclamation of disgust at something yucky

explanation.surface: Someone told to grow their hair long reacts with disgust at a half-cut style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' keeps LO of LONG; 'half cut' also reads as British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlough is a leave of absence, especially granted to a soldier or employee.

clue.text: Pass by instead crossing a pawn

indicators.note: crossing means the word for instead runs across, around the other letters

parts.note: else means otherwise, instead
P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess piece goes past, perhaps cutting across a pawn's path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts AP inside ELSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes by, a synonym for slipping away.

clue.text: See 17
See 17
Egg very round? On the contrary, I'm not sure

indicators.note: on the contrary means the order of very and round is switched round

parts.note: O is round in shape
um is the sound of hesitation, unsure

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over whether an egg is very round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very round' gives VO; 'On the contrary' reverses it to OV.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovum is a female egg cell, the biological term for an egg.

clue.text: Child pincher

definitions.meaning: informal British for a small child
something that nips or pinches, such as a crab's claw

explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is British slang for a young child, and literally one who nips, like a claw.

clue.text: Ultimately, black on black — something black or white

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word black

parts.note: night is black, dark

explanation.surface: A dark shade layered on dark, then something either colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. In chess the pieces are black or white.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is a chess piece, and chessmen come in black or white sets.
